statement: Every entry below is a blocker that the Phase160 hardening cycle did NOT resolve, each with the reason it cannot be resolved from inside this archive. None has been downgraded by wording, and none is a test that was silenced to make the suite look better. Phase160 was deliberately a hardening-only cycle: its scope was the scanner-model boundary declared by the Phase159 vendor-audit handoff, evidence-collection being external-blocked as below.

blockers.what: Five tests pin strategy digest c52e648c4e6a... (full value in the tests themselves) and still FAIL against this tree.
blockers.why: The digest matches no revision recoverable from this archive, from any archive on disk (Phase131..Phase159), or from the original upload. The documented contract in scripts/recertify_strategy_digest.py states the re-certification requires the original Git checkout plus a research re-execution it cannot perform here; it returns STATUS: BLOCKED.
blockers.effect: The five tests are correct change detectors and stay red on purpose. Re-pinning them to the current bytes would destroy the only evidence that the strategy changed; no phase has done that.
blockers.unblock: Recover the original Git history and re-execute the research path, then run the documented re-certification.

blockers.what: No funding-through-settlement capture exists for the hardened tree.
blockers.why: The capture needs an authorized Testnet order run. The India Testnet API key's IP whitelist still holds 157.33.197.21, so an authenticated request from the current egress address is refused before any order could be signed.
blockers.effect: The funding-cost component of the economics ledger remains INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. No order-capable script was run during Phase 160.
blockers.unblock: The operator removes or replaces the IP restriction on the India Testnet key, then authorizes a bounded run.

blockers.what: No second reconciled match exists beyond the two bounded captures already held.
blockers.why: Same external cause as BLOCK-160-02: the IP whitelist blocks the authorized order run the capture requires.
blockers.effect: The windowed reconciler (reconcile_with_rest_windowed, Phase157) is the strongest statement available: it certifies a WINDOW, never the account.

blockers.what: 40 Git-dependent facts are gated as BLOCKED_EVIDENCE: 19 that failed loudly in Phase157 and 21 that had been passing VACUOUSLY (a failed git command returns empty output, which satisfied assertEqual(out, "") / assertEqual(hits, [])).
blockers.why: No .git directory exists anywhere in this tree or in any archive delivered to it, so Git ancestry cannot be established in archive mode. The record was refreshed for this phase (reports/PHASE160_GIT_EVIDENCE_STATUS.json) with the fact set carried byte-for-byte from the Phase159 record; no gated test was added or removed by the hardening cycle.
blockers.effect: The release gate for ancestry stays BLOCKED, exactly as the Phase 2 requirement demands. The guard (tests/evidence_mode.py) steps aside in a real repository and was verified against a throwaway temp repo.
blockers.unblock: Deliver the project as a real Git repository (or record these facts as permanently inapplicable by an explicit contract change).

blockers.what: The Phase159 vendor-audit handoff WAS prepared on 2026-10-18 (PHASE159_AUDIT_HANDOFF.md, preserved with the superseded delivery in ../_phase159_superseded/): the materials table, the item-by-item brief substitution map, and the declaration of the scanner-model boundary this cycle closes. A vendor independent audit still has not happened for any phase of this chain.
blockers.why: Self-audit independence is by process only — the entity that produced the artifact cannot be independent of it by vendor. This block requires an auditor who did not build, repair, or ship the bytes.
blockers.effect: No self-produced report may be read as independent verification. A vendor receiving the Phase160 candidate must not inherit the Phase159 note's declared-boundary section as a standing condition: it is closed here (reports/PHASE160_HARDENING.json), and the closure claims are the thing to verify. A Phase160 handoff note has NOT been prepared — preparing it and engaging the auditor remain operator-attached steps.
blockers.unblock: Prepare the Phase160 handoff (same pattern as PHASE159_AUDIT_HANDOFF.md) and hand the archive + detached record + post-build bundle to an independent auditor; record the result.

blockers.what: Three advisory upgrades (python-dotenv 1.2.2, pyarrow 23.0.1, pytest 9.0.3) have been evaluated with zero new failures and remain deliberately NOT adopted into requirements.txt; the advisory list was re-verified by a fresh OSV query in this phase (reports/PHASE160_OSV_SCAN.json).
blockers.why: The pins are the reproducibility contract for every piece of evidence in this release; adopting a new environment requires re-deriving the evidence under it, which is its own deliberate step.
blockers.effect: The advisories remain open against the pinned versions. Two are unreachable from this codebase (re-verified by search in this tree); the third (pytest) affects local test execution only.
blockers.unblock: A phase whose scope includes re-deriving the evidence environment.

blockers.what: ADAUSD LONG 1 @ 0.23327 on the old account remains open and untouched by this phase.
blockers.why: Closing it requires operator funding and the old account's keys.
blockers.effect: Recorded here so it is not lost; Phase160 performed no order action of any kind.
blockers.unblock: Operator action on the old account.

standing_findings.statement: No economic edge is established for any strategy revision. This is unchanged by Phase160 and must be restated in any handoff: the release work repairs evidence integrity and hardens scanners, not profitability.

This archive deliberately contains raw private captures carrying the operator's account identifier and venue order ids (the value is parameterised in scripts/security/scan_privacy.py and appears nowhere but those captures). It is a restricted evidence package, not a distributable. See reports/PHASE160_PRIVACY_REVIEW.md. Test fixture identifiers are synthetic as of Phase159, and as of Phase160 every member is content-inspected or a declared opaque class.
